requirement.title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement.summary: MessagePackGenerator and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer throw IndexOutOfRangeException when collecting a closed generic value type declared in a referenced assembly. The crash prevents source generation and leaves the consuming app without GeneratedMessagePackResolver; the requested outcome is a clean build with the resolver generated.

criteria.text: Building `app` in the supplied two-project repro, where `lib` declares generic `record struct Item<T>` and `app` uses `Item<int>` as a member type through a `ProjectReference`, completes without CS8785 or an IndexOutOfRangeException from MessagePackGenerator.
criteria.summary: Repro builds with cross-project Item<int>, without CS8785 or generator crashes

criteria.text: Building that repro does not produce AD0001 caused by MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.
criteria.summary: Build produces no AD0001 from analyzer IndexOutOfRangeException

criteria.text: The MessagePack generator contributes output for `app`, and the built `app.dll` contains `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.
criteria.summary: Generator output includes GeneratedMessagePackResolver in built app.dll

criteria.text: The crash-free behavior also applies when the referenced generic value type is declared as plain `struct Item<T>` rather than `record struct Item<T>`, without moving it into `app` or adding a custom formatter.
criteria.summary: Plain struct Item<T> also builds across projects without custom formatter

criteria.text: The GetObjectInfo collection and diagnostic path reached for a closed generic metadata value type handles an empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences collection without indexing element 0 or throwing.
criteria.summary: GetObjectInfo handles empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences without indexing or throwing

open_questions: Which of the direct DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] accesses at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009, and 1101 actually throws in this repro?
requirement.short: MessagePackGenerator and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer must generate GeneratedMessagePackResolver for referenced closed generic value types

hunks.context: Two assembly-level attributes exist to help with mixing in your own custom forma
lines: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).

+Closed generic types defined in a referenced assembly (for example, `Item<int>` where `Item<T>` is defined in another project or NuGet package) can be used as members of your `[MessagePackObject]` types, including generic value types and record structs.
+Diagnostics about the members of such a type are reported by the assembly that defines it rather than by the consuming project, so any problem must be fixed there.

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
+This analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
+Members of a type defined in a referenced assembly are reported by the project that defines that type, so an unattributed public member of such a type must be fixed in its defining project.
